author: cskiraly
content:
While I agree it is good to have discussion here, I think there is a reason to limit it somehow. If people are allowed to post a zillion questions a day, and open the same amount of threads tagging others, then we are not doing work, just sitting in the noisy bar trying to chit-chat (or shouting at each other, depending on how heated the debate is 🙂 )

The point of having sync points and decisions processes is to avoid such distortions and allow real work to happen, without FOMO on the question of the moment.

I do agree with allowing posting opinion pieces as <@573787335796326400> said. (although I think the PQ specific part of the suggestion is only because of the channel we are in)

Posting them somewhere in this discord is way better than Twitter/X. Worth however noting that we already have ethresearch, magicians, spec repos with PRs, EIPs, and so on, so it can't be rationally expected that people doing work can also follow what's posted here.

author: ajsutton
content:
All the most interesting things come out of us disagreeing. 🙂  I wasn't pushing back on them because of a governance rule, just because we generally avoid self-promotion. I think these blog posts were pretty borderline - they were on topic and not just malicious spam, but at the same time they weren't responding to or creating conversation here. There are a LOT of articles written about topics we discuss here so if our policy is that its ok to just post them, we're going to get a lot of noise. ACD channel by contrast has a discussion about something or an upcoming meeting and people then share links to stuff they've written that furthers that discussion.

Not really sure how to define that line well though.

author: potuz
content: <@427491045308235776> The call was cut short but I also had <@194432762315407360> question, he asked why the use of a non-standardized function that is supported everywhere and instead of answering why this choice we heard that we anyway will have to keep previously used non-standard functions. I wanted to hear a reply to Felix's question, is there a benefit/reason to choose something non-standard? is it performance?

author: kevaundray
content:
Ah its not performance because keccak and sha3-256 only differ by 2 bits, so any cryptanalysis or acceleration for one carries over to the other. (at one point, we used to call keccak sha3)

I view the decision as whether we do keccak only or we do keccak plus sha3, since we cannot get rid of keccak. The main advantage to adding sha3 would be standardisation benefits like FIPS compliance, but our signature schemes are not standardised anyways. For example, the signature scheme is not SLH-DSA etc, so we would add another hash which differs by 2 bits for no benefit while also being confusing since they differ by only 2 bits.
